quote_text:
Yeah, it's obviously really disappointing.  That’s the second game in a row that we've  
dropped points, and the second game in a  row that, you know, in the first 45 minutes,  
we put ourselves in a position where we don’t  take full advantage. Then we're responding  
in the second half, and, you know, by  our standards, that's not good enough.
We’ve got to do a lot better than that.
Is that the thing that really hurts the most? 
Yeah, and it’s obviously, you know,  poor goals that we're giving away.
Yeah, we maybe created a couple of chances in  the first half but weren’t clinical enough. It’s  
obviously two different sides of football when  you see the first half compared to the second half  
today, and it’s completely different. We really  need to have a look at ourselves and address that.
What do you think is behind that? Well, obviously, we put ourselves on  
the back foot when we concede poor goals. That’s  effectively what’s happened in both games. You put  
yourself in a bad position, you know, you’re  going uphill to obviously get the goal back.
We started fairly okay, tried to move the ball,  
but obviously, there was more conviction  in the second half compared to the first.
Do you feel like the team hasn’t  started games the way it should? 
Yeah, and the first half of these last two  games is nothing compared to what we were  
playing beforehand—defending really well as  a team and not giving teams chances. But,  
you know, like today, we gave them away, and  we’ve been building something really good. Then,  
you know, the past two games, we’ve  just been giving sloppy goals away.
Do you feel like the team is  still running hard and trying? 
Well, if you look at the running stats,  
I don’t see any issue there. I see the  lads pushing completely to the end.
You’ve seen that today—the lads were pushing  completely to the end of the final whistle.  
But it’s obviously small details about not giving  goals away and being more clinical in their box.
I think we maybe rushed a bit too much  in the second half when, obviously,  
we got level. Maybe we could’ve asked  different questions, moved the ball a  
bit more around the box. It’s just those  small details that make the difference.
As a team, would someone put their hand  up and say, ‘I don’t feel 100% to play’  
like today, rather than letting the team down? You obviously want everyone to be honest. I think  
everyone will always be honest in the team and  always try and give their all every single time.
It’s just smaller things in how we concede these  goals. You know, we’ve got to do better on that.
Next up is an Old Firm  game—how do you approach that? 
It’s obviously against our biggest rivals and  a home game, so we obviously have to go back  
to what we were doing better before these  two games. That’s playing better as a team,  
performing as a team, defending  as a team, and being clinical.
The gap at the top is significant. Is that  something that feels unassailable at this point? 
It’s obviously a gap that we’re not happy about,  
but we’re just going to push all  the way to the end of the season.
How do you approach the next  game, given the recent results? 
We were unlucky in the final, going all  the way to extra time. We’re just going  
to go into that game and obviously need to  address what we need to do before Thursday  
and really look at ourselves as men  and as a team to put things right.
Some of the reaction online has suggested  there’s a lot of pressure on the manager’s  
shoulders. Do you feel that? I can only apologize to the  
supporters because, you know, the past  two games, we’ve wasted 90 minutes on  
two halves where the performance level  is not us, and that’s unacceptable.
So, you can understand the boos.  We set standards, and we’ve got to  
maintain those standards.  If we don’t, then, you know,  
they’re fully in their right to let us know. We  all know that, and we knew it wasn’t good enough.
This is the thing—we just can’t waste time on the  pitch. We’ve got to be at it for 90 minutes plus.
Is there still belief in the manager? Well, obviously, he’s our manager,  
and we obviously play for him to the end.
We’re going to fight for the shirt,  
but we obviously need to look  at ourselves and address it.
Thanks, guys. Thank you very much.
title: James Tavernier FULL Post Match Reaction | Motherwell 2-2 Rangers
